expectedMisconceptions: Small imprecision in angle measurement can go unnoticed by a child, even though it may change the interpreted pattern — worth double-checking a couple of key angles together.
Recognising a constellation's shape can get treated as the same skill as reading a star map's positional information, when the mission actually asks for both separately.
stretchQuestions: If your measured angles were slightly different, would your interpretation change? How sensitive is your conclusion to small measurement errors?
What do you think made this pattern important enough for the expedition to track for so long?
estimatedSupervision: Light — a protractor is useful for the angle-measuring step; a real star map or night-sky app can enrich the session if available, per the mission's own parent guide.
